title: Silent tenant metrics and intermittent dashboard zeros due to ingestion re-ordering
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported that per-tenant dashboards intermittently displayed zeroed time-series for key metrics (request_count, token_cost, latency_p50) during a 6-hour window. Traces for affected requests were present, but links from dashboard tiles to trace detail returned 404 or showed incomplete spans. The issue surfaced during a high-ingest period with autoscaling events and coincided with a single-customer private deployment lag in the read replica cluster.
impact_details: Customers: 3 Dedicated customers and 1 Private on-prem cluster. Symptom: dashboards showing sustained zeros for 5-20 minute windows for tenant-scoped metrics; alerts were missed. Business impact: customer-facing dashboards and some SLO reports were inaccurate; two customers escalated to SEs during the incident.
timeline_summary: 2025-03-12 09:13 - Pager triggered from tenant-monitoring. 09:18 - SE triage confirmed dashboard zeros; alerting pipelines showed reduced ingestion. 09:30 - Eng oncall started investigation. 10:05 - Identified correlation with a large write-batch and recent ingestion change (reordering optimization deployed in runtime-1.17). 11:20 - Hotpatch rolled (PR #7890) to disable reordering for tenant-scoped writes and rehydrate tombstones; partial recovery observed. 13:00 - Read-repair job run for affected tenants. 15:10 - Full dashboards recovered. 2025-03-20 - Root cause postmortem and follow-ups completed.
root_cause: A recently introduced ingestion re-ordering optimization intended to improve batching latencies allowed dependent metric write events to be applied out-of-order in the tenant index when a tombstone (TTL-based deletion) raced with an incoming update. In high-throughput bursts the metric index occasionally wrote a tombstone after a later write because batching committed segments non-atomically across the index and the time-based eviction logic used wall-clock checks instead of a monotonic event ordering. The result: the metric series existed in storage but the index exposed it as deleted, causing live-panel queries to return zeros and breaking trace->metric link resolution.
fix_summary: 1) Hotpatch (PR #7890) to temporarily disable the re-ordering optimization for tenant-scoped ingestion and to make tombstone writes idempotent. 2) Read-repair job (job ID: rr-2025-03-12-01) that reconciled index state for affected tenant time windows. 3) Permanent fix (PR #7924) implemented atomic commit semantics for index segment writes and switched eviction checks to event-sequence based ordering. 4) Added a canary ingestion test and an e2e dashboard smoke test to catch regressions before rollout.
engineering_changes: PR #7890: emergency rollback logic and tombstone idempotency (merged 2025-03-12). PR #7924: atomic index segment commit + sequence-numbered eviction and unit tests (merged 2025-03-18). PR #7941: read-repair scheduler and admin endpoint (merged 2025-03-16). Added ingestion-canary pipeline in CI (pipeline id: canary-ingest-3).
deployment_and_rollback: Hotpatch rolled to dedicated clusters at 10:05 UTC (progressive rollout to all dedicated pools in 30m). Read-repair run completed by 13:00 UTC. No rollback required after stabilization; permanent fix rolled as a controlled canary on 2025-03-17 and full rollout completed 2025-03-18.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: New metrics added: ingest.write_reorder_disabled_count, index.tombstone_conflict_count, read_repair.jobs_run. Alert thresholds: index.tombstone_conflict_count > 0 for 3m alerts on P1. Dashboard smoke test job added to critical path for canary clusters; daily health-check that queries tenant sample dashboards and validates non-zero responses.
customer_communications: SEs notified impacted customers 2025-03-12 14:30 UTC with interim mitigation details. Stand-up postmortem and RCA shared via Confluence link. Offer extended log export for impacted tenants and a 1:1 follow-up for the Private customer experiencing replica lag.
follow_ups_and_action_items: 1) ENG: Finish index refactor to support multi-segment atomic commits (owner: Ethan Liu, due 2025-04-02). 2) PM: Update SLO docs to include dashboard-data freshness window (owner: Priya Menon, due 2025-03-28). 3) DX: Add tenant-scoped dashboard smoke tests to onboarding templates (owner: Carlos Rivera, due 2025-03-31). 4) Reliability: Add periodic read-repair sweeper for orphaned metric series (owner: Mei Chen, due 2025-04-10).
playbook_updates: Updated runbook section 'dashboard-zeros' with triage steps, commands to run read-repair, and indicators to flip ingestion reordering toggle. Playbook version: 2025.03.20.
tests_added: Unit tests for atomic segment commits; integration test that emits tombstones and out-of-order updates; CI canary that runs tenant-dashboard smoke test on every canary build.
post_release_validation: After full rollout, we monitored index.tombstone_conflict_count and ingest success for 72 hours across dedicated and private clusters. No recurrence in 30 days.
retrospective_notes: The re-ordering optimization lacked a tenant-scoped invariants checklist and insufficiently considered TTL/tombstone interactions. We will gate similar low-level ingest optimizations behind a checklist and mandatory canary with synthetic tombstone scenarios.
